operations.title: Add production VM
operations.summary: Allocate the next prodN, install its OS, replicate it, and enable HA.
operations.description: Allocates the next prodN, installs its OS, verifies the guest's identity through the guest agent, creates replication to every selected placement host, configures HA, and publishes its routes. It can resume its own incomplete allocation after a failure. Start with a dry run.

operations.title: Remove production VM
operations.summary: Permanently destroy a production VM and everything BMAC owns for it.
operations.description: Permanently removes one production VM after exact identity validation: routes, HA resource and rule, replication jobs and target copies, the VM and its volumes, orchestration metadata, and its registry allocation. Staging VMs derived from it must be removed first.

operations.title: Move production VM
operations.summary: Relocate a production VM to another of its placement hosts.
operations.description: Determines the VM's real HA owner, replicates the latest changes to the chosen placement host, and relocates the VM there. The application is briefly unavailable while the VM restarts. Staging VMs on the new owner are evicted.
operations.notes: The adapted script takes the VM as --resource instead of asking for it.

operations.title: Change placement
operations.summary: Add or remove the hosts a production VM replicates to and may run on.
operations.description: Adds placement hosts (replicating the VM there before HA may use them) or removes them (never the live owner, keeping at least two). Detects and finishes a partial earlier change.
operations.notes: The adapted script takes the VM as --resource instead of asking for it.

operations.title: Grow production disk
operations.summary: Grow a production VM's root disk online.
operations.description: Calculates how much the VM's root zvol may grow while every placement pool keeps 10% free, grows it on the live owner, replicates the new size, and grows the guest's filesystem online.
operations.notes: The adapted script takes the VM as --resource instead of asking for it.

operations.title: Add staging VM
operations.summary: Create a production-derived linked-clone staging VM.
operations.description: Snapshots a production VM, waits for the snapshot to replicate to a standby host, and creates a stopped stageNprodN linked clone there with a new machine identity. When the production VM already has staging VMs, it lists them and offers to share one of their snapshots instead of taking a new one. Optionally starts it. Start with a dry run.
operations.notes: The adapted script takes the production VM as --source instead of asking for it. v2's --sanitizer took a workstation path; how a sanitizer reaches the host is decided in M4.3.

operations.title: Remove staging VM
operations.summary: Destroy a staging VM, its clone, and its unshared source snapshot.
operations.description: Permanently removes a staging VM's route, VM and disks, and linked clone. Its source snapshot is deleted too unless another staging VM still shares it; a shared snapshot is deleted with the last staging VM using it. Production itself is never touched.

operations.title: Remove Proxmox host
operations.summary: Remove a host gracefully, or forcefully when it is permanently dead.
operations.description: Removes a host gracefully when it can be contacted and nothing depends on it, or forcefully when it cannot be contacted and has been permanently disconnected. Forced removal narrows affected production placement and destroys related staging VMs.

operations.title: Add QDevice
operations.summary: Add an external tie-breaking vote to an even-sized cluster.
operations.description: Checks that the cluster needs a QDevice, verifies SSH to the prepared QDevice machine, installs corosync-qnetd there, pins its host key on every host, and runs pvecm qdevice setup.

operations.title: Remove QDevice
operations.summary: Remove the QDevice gracefully, or evict a failed one forcefully.
operations.description: Removes a reachable QDevice gracefully and uninstalls its software. When it is inaccessible, offers to evict it forcefully without contacting it, after you confirm it was removed from Tailscale.

params.label: QDevice SSH host
params.help: Defaults to the QDevice host in the cluster settings.

operations.title: Cluster health check
operations.summary: Hosts, corosync links, QDevice, every ZFS member, free space, and SMART.
operations.description: Inspects every host directly (or through another member), every corosync link between hosts, the QDevice, every ZFS pool and vdev member with disk serials, rpool free space, and each drive's SMART health. Guests are not inspected. Takes a minute or more.

operations.title: Full cluster state
operations.summary: Exhaustive read-only report of every host, the QDevice, and the registry.
operations.description: Runs the complete read-only diagnostic snapshot on every reachable host and the QDevice: identity, networking, SSH trust, quorum, services, ISO readiness, HA, replication, ZFS, LUKS, SMART, boot, nftables, HAProxy, and the shared registry. Produces a very long report and takes several minutes.

operations.title: Inspect a host
operations.summary: One host's configuration, guests, replicas, and rpool layout with disk serials.
operations.description: Shows one Proxmox host's configuration, the guests it runs and the replicas it stores, and its rpool layout: every vdev resolved to physical disk serials, the boot/ESP vdev, device-removal progress, unused disks, and per-zvol usage.

operations.title: Inspect a production VM
operations.summary: One production VM across HA, replication, routing, storage, and the guest agent.
operations.description: Checks one registered production VM without changing guest, Proxmox, HA, replication, route, or registry configuration.

operations.title: Inspect the QDevice
operations.summary: Whether a QDevice is needed, registered, alive, and voting on every host.
operations.description: Reports whether the cluster needs an external QDevice, whether one is registered, and whether every member sees it alive and voting, and explains how to repair or replace it.
